elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 as rendered contains no affiliate carve-out; the only no-consent route is "merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement". An affiliate transfer would still require Vendor's prior written consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: "either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent upon written notice to the other party" — Customer is within "either party" (subject only to the reciprocal direct-competitor consent proviso).

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: "Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party" binds Vendor symmetrically.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Inserted language: "without the prior written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld."

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The retained proviso only conditions a competitor transaction on consent ("except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party where consent of the other party will be required"), and that consent is now subject to a reasonableness standard; there is no absolute prohibition on assignment to a Customer competitor.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Nothing in Section 14.1 as rendered, or in the cited record, confers a Vendor termination or re-pricing right on Customer's change of control; the clause treats a change-of-control transfer only as an assignment question. Condition therefore does not arise.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: Pre-existing mutual carve-out retained: "either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent"; the direct-competitor proviso is a narrow reciprocal condition and does not remove the mutual successor right.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted "upon written notice to the other party" attaches directly to the successor/M&A no-consent right.

"Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party"; the only no-consent exception retained is the successor/M&A route — there is no affiliate or other non-successor no-consent exception, and "Any assignment in violation of this Section 14.1 shall be null and void" is preserved.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Inserted "which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld" qualifies the general consent requirement in the first sentence, which governs all non-successor assignments.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the two insertions ("which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld" and "upon written notice to the other party") supply the only two fallback elements the original lacked, while mutual successor assignment and the consent requirement for other assignments were already present.

Preferred is not reached: no Customer affiliate no-consent carve-out, and the competitor restriction is only a consent trigger rather than an absolute bar on Vendor assignment to a Customer competitor. To reach preferred the drafter would need to add an express Customer right to assign to an affiliate without consent and convert the competitor proviso into a flat prohibition on Vendor assignment to a Customer competitor.

Minimality holds: no words were deleted, no survival tails, procedures, or extraneous obligations were added, and the reasonableness standard was placed on the existing consent sentence rather than by way of a broad notwithstanding override.

Intent preserved: the direct-competitor consent proviso, the successors-and-permitted-assigns binding sentence, and the null-and-void remedy all survive without contradiction; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are introduced.

Classification as "deviation" is supportable — pre-edit the clause failed two material fallback terms (no reasonableness standard on consent, no notice mechanic) — though the gap was narrow and non-walk-away, since no Vendor change-of-control termination or re-pricing right appears.
